meta.title: Assessment and inventory | Audit & Report
meta.description: The Audit & Report assessment: report profiles, how results are classified, accepted risks, unreadable sources, Lynis and the inventory of the node.

header.title: Assessment and inventory
header.description: The assessment inspects the node, keeps its findings and answers different questions depending on the report profile.

calloutInfo.title: An assessment inspects; it does not change the configuration
calloutInfo.body: It reads the configuration and state of the host. It writes its results, reports and logs, and the boot checks can mount EFI system partitions for a moment. The configuration it assesses is not modified.

blocks.p: Run assessment starts a run with the profile selected in Report. The view shows the date of the last run and how long ago it was.

sections.title: Report profiles
sections.intro: Each profile answers a different question. The checks and sections are selected before the document is composed.

rows: Every check and all the structure available.
Every check; the result opens with the critical findings, the warnings and the readings that could not be verified.
A description of the node, with no checks and no classification.
Exposure, access, privileges, certificates, updates, repositories and Lynis.
Coverage, age, results, verification, retention and recovery of the backups.
Growth margin, memory, space usage and the service life of the disks.

blocks.p: The contents of each document are described in <reportsLink>Reports and comparisons</reportsLink>.

rows: A failed condition that has priority.
A condition that needs a review, given the evidence or the policy.
Information about the node that is not reported as a failure.
The source the check needs could not be read. It does not mean the problem is absent.
The condition meets the criterion applied.
Nothing within the scope of the check applies.
The finding exists and a decision about it has been recorded.
The policy declares that the element is left out of the count.

blocks.p: Findings can be filtered by area: System, Storage, Network, Security, Backup, Guests and Hardware. Each finding keeps its evidence, with the source it was read from.

sections.title: When a source cannot be read

rows: The check keeps its identity, states in its evidence which source failed and does not turn missing data into a conformant result.
The report names the source and the time of collection, so a real problem can be told apart from an insufficient reading.
Once the access, package or service is corrected, the same profile runs again and the comparison shows whether the result could be verified.

blocks.p: The security review uses the Lynis report of the host. When Lynis has not been run yet, or its report is older than the threshold of the policy, a dialog offers Run with Lynis, which takes a few minutes longer, or Run without Lynis, which uses the existing report.

figure.alt: Dialog that offers to run the assessment with or without Lynis
figure.caption: The Lynis dialog before a security review.

blocks.p: Accept risk records a decision on a finding. The reason is required and is stored with the author and the date.

rows: 90 days, 180 days, 1 year or does not expire. When the period ends the finding becomes active again.
A reminder that brings the decision back to attention while it stays in force.

blocks.p: An accepted finding stays visible with its decision, and Return to active revokes it. An accepted risk is not a correction: the comparison reports it as accepted, not as resolved.

items: Identity, Proxmox VE version, kernel, subscription and cluster.
CPU, memory, board, BIOS, controllers and IOMMU.
Disks, SMART, power-on hours and recorded events.
Adapters, bonds, bridges, latency and connections.
Storage, guests with their disks and interfaces, and backups.
PCI passthrough and the software ProxMenux manages.
